For each question, let \(I\) be the set of people who answered it incorrectly.

- Since any group of 5 answered all questions, no 5 people can all be incorrect on the same question, so \(|I|\le 4\).
- Since any group of 4 fails to answer all questions, for every 4-person subset \(T\), there must be a question whose incorrect set contains \(T\).

But if \(|I|\le 4\) and \(T\subseteq I\) with \(|T|=4\), then \(I=T\). Thus each question can cover exactly one 4-person subset.

There are \(\binom{10}{4}=210\) four-person subsets, and they can be covered by 210 questions, one for each subset where exactly those four answer incorrectly.

\[
\boxed{210}
\]
